detail:
# Recommendation — an audit for the Pi agent config directory

**What.** `~/.pi/agent` is a mutable, ungated config directory that at least
three unrelated installers write into (a desktop app, an npm package manager, and
a skills marketplace). On 2026-10-11 a tidy removed 19 skill entries and 17
backup files, none of which any gate had noticed arriving. Nothing measures that
they are gone, and nothing will measure it when they return. Propose a lint —
`just pi-audit` here, backed by `scripts/audit-pi-config.ts` — with three checks.

**Why this repo owns it.** `decisions/013-silo-exception-pi-config.md` already
makes this repo the sole explicit owner of `~/.pi/agent/models.json` and
`~/.pi/agent/settings.json`. An audit that dereferences those paths is the same
exception applied as a gate instead of a permission — and it is the natural home
for the "does the config resolve?" question that no other silo can answer.

## The three checks

**1. Every path in `settings.json` resolves.** `skills`, `extensions` and
`packages` must dereference. Found 2026-10-11:
`"skills": ["+../../.agents/skills/find-skills/SKILL.md"]` pointed at a directory
that had been deleted at some earlier date — an *exact inclusion* (the `+` form,
`docs/settings.md:158`) resolving to nothing, silently. The entry is now removed,
but the class of defect survives: nothing read that path to check it.

**2. Every advertised skill has a live referent.** Pi scans
`~/.pi/agent/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, project `.agents/skills/` through
its ancestors, and package `skills/` directories (`docs/skills.md:59-63`).
Tally on 2026-10-11 before the tidy: 19 entries — 10 real directories (9 in
`~/.agents/skills/` plus `supacode-cli` in `~/.pi/agent/skills/`) and 9
symlinks — of which one was a **broken symlink** (`cua-driver` →
`/Applications/CuaDriver.app/Contents/Resources/Skills/cua-driver`, absent) and
none was authored in this silo. Nine of the ten directories arrived from
`anthropics/skills`, `vercel-labs/agent-browser` and `zencoderai/skills` per
`~/.agents/skills/.manifest.json`; the tenth is written by a desktop app.
An advertised skill whose file is gone is a citation that does not resolve, and
the reader of the system prompt cannot tell.

**3. No un-git'd backups in `~/.pi/agent`.** The directory is **not a git repo**
(`git -C ~/.pi/agent rev-parse` → "not a git repository"), so the 17
`*.bak` / `*.pre-llama-*` / `*.ollama-*` files were its hand-rolled history.
That is *references, not recitals* in file form: git is the memory, and a `.bak`
is a second copy no gate can check and no one re-reads. One of them
(`AGENTS.md.bak-2026-10-08`, 131 lines) is **not** identical to the git-held
`SYSTEM.md` — a protocol revision that existed only as a backup. Either git-init
the agent directory or declare its state disposable; but pick one, because
seventeen backups is not a policy.

## Also for your awareness

- **`~/.workbuddy-ai/skills/`** holds 10 `okuda-*` skills, outside every path Pi
  scans. The okuda silo already named this defect (*the relocation flag*,
  `okuda/docs/2026-09-18-continuity-by-re-reading.md:172-173`). Same class as the
  above: a parallel store with no gate and no register.
- **`~/.pi/agent/agents/`** held six agent definitions, removed 2026-10-11, with
  no consumer — Pi's own docs never mention a subagent facility
  (`grep -rln subagent docs/` → nothing) and no extension read the directory.
  `visual-tester.md:6` named skill `chrome-cdp`, which exists nowhere on disk.
- **Supacode will probably put `~/.pi/agent/skills/supacode-cli` back.** Its Pi
  extension (`extensions/supacode/index.ts`) and that skill share mtime
  `Jun 18 18:11`, so the app believes it owns a path inside Pi's config. If a
  fourth installer can write there, check 2 is not a one-off tidy — it is a
  recurring lint.

**Removal record, for the receiver's confidence.** Everything removed is staged in
`~/.Trash/pi-skills-tidy-2026-10-11/` and `~/.Trash/pi-agent-tidy-2026-10-11/` —
recoverable, not destroyed. Skill provenance is preserved as
`skills-manifest.json.bak` and `skill-lock.json.bak`, so reinstallation from
upstream is a command rather than an archaeology. Symlink targets
(`~/.understand-anything/repo/…`, `CuaDriver.app`) were left untouched.
